first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because the brand is on our planner shortlist and the honeymoon is the part we haven't handed to anyone yet. The first screen is calm and not pushy, which I'll give them. But it opens on getting the fee and inclusions in writing, and that tells me in seconds the page is for a couple watching costs. Her summary: a tidy guide to what a honeymoon planner does, two lines on Wedded Concierge, a section on passports and name changes, and a list of consumer questions about insurance, insolvency and exchange rates. I read the intro and the Wedded Advisor section and stopped. She skimmed the rest.

journey.quote: The good ones agree their fee and confirm what is included in writing before you commit to anything.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but it's the second sentence on the page and it's about protecting yourself from the bill. That's not what I'm judging a planner on. I want to know what they can arrange.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: You describe the shape of it: how long you have, the kind of places that make you both exhale, the one thing you will not go without.
journey.reaction: This is the right tone. Understated, about how it should feel. More of this, please.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: Australian consumer guarantees apply whether you book directly with an airline or tour operator, through a travel agent, or through a booking platform or package provider.
journey.reaction: A booking platform or package provider is not the comparison I'm making. The family office handles our rights. My assistant moved on.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: You meet your Wedded Advisor, one person who stays with you to the end.
journey.reaction: For a honeymoon, one person is exactly what I want. Fewer people knowing where we are and when is better. I'd just want to know how discreet that person and the bookings are.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.
journey.reaction: The fee in writing has now come up three times before I've read a word about where they could take us. It reads as reassurance for someone nervous about money.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Travel can be planned anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Good. We split our time between Dubai, Sydney and London, so that matters more to me than the AUD line before it.

journey.section: Planning the honeymoon alongside your wedding
journey.quote: Planning them as two separate projects means two sets of contacts, two sets of deadlines and two lots of quotes in foreign currencies to convert at the kitchen table.
journey.reaction: The idea is right, one team across the wedding and the honeymoon. 'Converting at the kitchen table' isn't my life, though. It pulls the page back down.

journey.section: What to decide before you enquire
journey.quote: A pool you never have to share. A night somewhere very remote.
journey.reaction: This is the closest the page gets to us. Privacy and seclusion are the brief. I wish it went further, to whole villas, private islands, private transfers.

journey.section: What to decide before you enquire
journey.quote: Think about how you would like to pay, in what order and on what card, before the first deposit is due.
journey.reaction: Which card? Our office pays. This is budget-traveller advice.

journey.section: What to decide before you enquire
journey.quote: If you would like a starting point to react to, our [honeymoon packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-honeymoon-packages) show the kind of itineraries couples begin from.
journey.reaction: Packages. That's the word that tells me I'd be treated like every other enquiry.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: Agent insolvency is commonly excluded from cancellation cover, and insolvency insurance is not compulsory for agents, so only some have it.
journey.reaction: If I'm worrying about whether my planner goes bust, I've chosen the wrong planner. Seven questions about fees, insurance and exchange rates make the brand feel like a mid-market agency.

unanswered_questions: How do they keep our names, dates and locations confidential with hotels, airlines and staff?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a villa or small island, private aviation and private transfers?
Can they work with our own security team at each stay?
Is the same team that plans the wedding planning the honeymoon, and who is on the ground if something changes?
Is there a private or referral route to someone senior, rather than a web form?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would like a starting point to react to, our [honeymoon packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-honeymoon-packages) show the kind of itineraries couples begin from.
turn_offs_found.why: Package language. It suggests a catalogue to pick from, which is exactly how I don't want to be treated.

turn_offs_found.quote: Think about how you would like to pay, in what order and on what card, before the first deposit is due.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining money in a way that frames the reader as budget-conscious.

turn_offs_found.quote: So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.
turn_offs_found.why: Repeated cost reassurance (intro, takeaways, this section, closing). The repetition reads as eager and value-led rather than about what's possible.

would_share_with: My assistant might forward the 'one person who stays with you to the end' and 'anywhere in the world' lines to the family office as a note on the brand. Not the page itself.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [speak with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planning-service&utm_content=closing) and tell us anything.
cta_reaction.why: 'Tell us anything' is warm and I don't mind it. But nothing here speaks to privacy, exclusive use or discretion, and I wouldn't enquire through a blog link anyway. A honeymoon is a smaller, lower-risk way to try a planner than the wedding itself, so if they came through a referral I might give them this first.

top_3_changes: In 'What to decide before you enquire', reword or move the honeymoon packages line (for example 'our honeymoon itineraries show where couples often begin') so the section about privacy and must-haves doesn't end on package language.

In 'What to decide before you enquire', drop 'and on what card' from the pace of payment point, and in 'Planning the honeymoon alongside your wedding' replace 'convert at the kitchen table' with something neutral, so the page doesn't frame every reader as budget-led.

In 'Tell us anything' or the closing section, add one line inviting couples to mention privacy, security or exclusive-use needs at first contact, so readers like me know the conversation can start there.
